about: The Model requests' kinds, as the window's tabs: each made as one of the kit's eight (made_as: how the kit makes it and what it becomes in the game), the settings its requests are asked (params, from the window's own: height, cells, style, pose, shapes, bones, variants, many, check_lines), its instructions (features: a keyword and how a run handles it, each a line of every run's prompt) and its varieties (each with its own params and instructions, added to the kind's: one with the same keyword replaces the kind's; made as its kind unless it says how, made_as). The catalogue's own features go with every request, whatever its kind (a kind's with the same keyword replaces one). A character's creature variety makes a creature of the fields (its prop's category creature, a creature record of its own in the editor); grass, a flower, a rock and a tree are the environment's varieties, each made its own way. The editor edits this file on the desktop; a browser keeps its own copy (private/requests/kinds.json), which its runs are given.

features.text: what the wind moves painted for it
its blades (or leaves) evenly dense right up to the borders, none past them, no bare margin and no soil or base showing at an edge: copies in the cells side by side join without a gap
each blade or leaf a piece of its own, none heavy, not one mesh joined up
as dense and fine as the pictures want, within its vertex budget
kit.tube along a gentle curve, tapering up to the head, a node or two where its leaves grow
thin slabs bent along their length and cupped, each from a node or a rosette at its foot
each its own thin curved surface: cupped, curving out, its tip curling, in rings that overlap, the inner ones smaller; each petal's colour shading along it as the design does
a disc, a dome or a cone, with stamens where the design has them (long thin filaments fanning out of it, each tipped with an anther), and the sepals under the head
painted in one kit.plant_wind call: the stem as stems, rooted at its foot, the petals and the leaves fluttering
as fine as the design: its mass, then its facets, cracks, ledges and strata
varying over it: paint volumes for veins, lichen and weathering, or a texture painted from the pictures
in patches where moss grows: its top, its shaded side, its hollows and cracks
grass and flowers at its foot and out of its cracks where the design has them, each blade or stem a thin piece of its own, painted for the wind (the rock never)
its trunk and its main branches are meshes: the trunk tapering from its foot, forking into a few branches (two to five) that reach into the foliage

clusters of leaves, each cluster a few curved planes (3 or 4 cards, bent a little, crossing at the cluster's middle at different angles), each card's outline cut to the leaves' silhouette (a scalloped, leafy edge) in the mesh itself: crossed cards read as a cluster from every side; as many clusters as the crown's shape asks, each on a branch or in reach of one
the leaves' colour, darker toward a cluster's underside and lighter on top; two-sided as a leaf is
the trunk rooted (0 at its foot, a little at its top), the branches more, the clusters most, their flutter on the cards; a phase of its own per cluster, so the crown doesn't move as one block
